images.caption: Caol Rona Bothy. The ruins marked on the OS map here as sheilings (seasonal grazings)were in fact permanent croft houses built by the poor souls that were cleared brutally by the landowners from the more fertile crofts of South Raasay. This one has been made into a first class bothy.

images.caption: Inside Church Cave, Rona. The cave was once used as a church by local people. The square stone in the centre was the altar and other stones were set inside the cave to act as pews.  A wooden box containing a bible still remains in the heart of the cave.
images.alt: Inside Church Cave, Rona. The cave was once used as a church by local people. The square stone in the centre was the altar and other stones were set inside the cave to act as pews.  A wooden box containing a bible still remains in the heart of the cave.
